why:
The criterion holds for all four checks. I compared each check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line.

Check 1 only tests that clamp is exported and returns x, lo or hi as the words require. The lo===hi case [3,3,3,3] is still a range from lo to hi, so it isn't stricter.

Check 2 only tests that lo > hi throws a RangeError.

Check 3 uses a heading-matching script, but it adds "judge by the README's content" when a function is documented in another form. Its PASS condition is just "every exported function is described in README.md", so no heading format is required.

Check 4 asks for "exit code 0 and the summary shows fail 0". With `node --test` this is the same as the suite passing. It's a borderline extra format requirement, but it doesn't test anything beyond the words.

The stricter items (new clamp tests, add/subtract/multiply unchanged) are under "Advisory (does not affect PASS/FAIL)".
